correctness.rationale: Every positive sphere f is uniquely f_{h,a} where h=f(0)+f' has sup-norm one and 0<=a<=min h. The positive-sum norm is exactly the sup norm of profile sums; peak-function tests imply equal positive-sum profiles exactly when h coincides. Thus an onto norm-additive T induces an onto norm-additive map of the positive C(I) unit sphere. The full proof of Ezumi–Miura Theorem 2.1 provides a unique homeomorphism tau on profiles, and ontoness makes each remaining interval map psi_h onto. The explicit formula verifies its own positivity, norm, surjectivity and preservation converse, including min h=0 and h=1; no numerical or infinite-computational claim.

value.rationale: The complete natural all-surjective-maps classification fills the structural gap left by a current endpoint counterexample: quotient automorphisms are exactly interval homeomorphisms while all freedom is localized to arbitrary interval fiber surjections. It gives necessary-and-sufficient parametrization and exact bijection criterion without extra regularity assumptions, sharply contrasting endpoint flexibility with the proven \(p>1\) rigidity. It is not a numerical improvement or an arbitrary slice; the stated scope and use of the published auxiliary theorem are explicit.
